title: Thirty-Nine Delegates Sign the US Constitution in Philadelphia
dek: On 17 September 1787 the Philadelphia Convention signs a charter for a stronger national government and sends it to the states, opening the fight between Federalists and Anti-Federalists.
body: It needed nine of thirteen states. Federalists won ratification by June 1788; Anti-Federalists won the Bill of Rights in 1791.

panels.label: The Federalists Said
panels.text: Federalists such as Madison said a Congress that could not tax risked national bankruptcy and break-up, and that a large republic with a stronger national government would check faction.

panels.label: The Anti-Federalists Said
panels.text: Anti-Federalists led by Patrick Henry said the charter would erode state sovereignty and individual liberty, that the presidency could grow into a monarchy, and that it lacked a bill of rights.

panels.label: The Stakes
panels.text: Both sides claimed the Revolution's legacy; at stake was whether the power to tax, regulate trade and make war would sit with a national government or stay with the states.
